articles.title: Siri AI's Biggest Upgrade Yet + John Ternus's First Apple Earnings Call
articles.content: Apple is finally bringing some of Siri's most ambitious AI capabilities to the iPhone. In this episode of Power On, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman and Vlad Savov break down the major changes coming with iOS 27.3, including Siri's new ability to control apps, carry out complex tasks and coordinate actions across multiple applications. They discuss how these improvements compare with AI agents from OpenAI and Meta, and why Apple still has a long way to go. Plus, Mark and Vlad analyze John Ternus's first earnings call as Apple's CEO, the company's strong iPhone sales, concerns about slowing growth and profit margins, and why more price increases could be coming. They also examine Apple's AI rollout in China and the privacy implications of new always-listening Apple Watch features. Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 12499 元 / 15999 元起：苹果 M6 芯片款 iMac、MacBook Pro 开售
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，苹果 M6 芯片款 iMac、MacBook Pro 今日正式开售，起售价分别为 12499 元 / 15999 元，国补后起售价约 10999 元 / 14499 元。如果您能使用教育优惠，叠加国补后起售价会进一步下探至 10599 元 / 13699 元。京东 Apple iMac M6  12499 元直达链接京东 Apple MacBook Pro M6 14 英寸 15999 元直达链接IT之家附两款新品详情如下：iMac新款 iMac 沿袭上一代外观，提供银色、蓝色、绿色、粉色等配色可选。搭载 24 英寸 4.5K 分辨率屏幕，最高亮度 500nits，支持 P3 广色域和 10bit 色深，提供纳米纹理玻璃选项。规格方面，新款 iMac 搭载 M6 芯片，双雷雳接口机型为 10 核 CPU、10 核 GPU 及双 16 核 NPU；四雷雳接口型号采用 12 核 CPU、12 核心 GPU 及双 16 核 NPU。标配 16GB 统一内存，可选 24GB 或 32GB。硬盘为 256GB 起步，可选 512GB/1TB/2TB。此外，新 iMac 搭载 Apple N1 无线网络芯片、支持 Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) 和蓝牙 6。支持选配 2.5Gb 以太网端口，出厂搭载 macOS 操作系统。MacBook Pro新款 M6 芯片的 14 英寸 MacBook Pro 继承了上一代外观，可选深空黑色和银色两种配色，配备 3024 x 1964 分辨率 120Hz 显示屏。这款电脑搭载 M6 芯片，为 12 核中央处理器、12 核图形处理器、双 16 核神经网络引擎规格，官方称该机设备端 AI 性能相对于 13 英寸 M1 机型最高提速至 13 倍。同时，新款 M6 芯片的 14 英寸 MacBook Pro 机型内存带宽达 170GB/s，比 M5 机型的 153GB/s 有所提升，但性能提升并未延伸到基础款的 16GB 统一内存配置。技术规格页面显示，16GB 统一内存的选项仍然限制在 153GB/s。与 M5 机型相同，而只有全新的 24GB 和 32GB 配置才拥有更快的 170GB/s 内存带宽。作为对比，搭载 M5 Pro 芯片的 MacBook Pro 提供 307GB/s 的内存带宽，而搭载 M5 Max 芯片的机型则具有高达 614GB/s 的内存带宽。京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 荣耀 700 系列手机盲盒周边曝光：背屏设计确认，消息称标准版搭载骁龙 8s Gen4 处理器

articles.title: One UI 9 系统更新导致部分 Galaxy 手机无法连接 Wi-Fi 或识别 SIM 卡，三星暂未回应
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，据科技媒体 Android Headline 今天报道，部分 Galaxy 手机用户升级 One UI 9 正式版系统后遭遇大范围网络故障，导致无法连接 Wi-Fi 或无法识别 SIM 卡。重启设备只能暂时缓解故障。IT之家从原报道获悉，许多三星用户已经在反馈，他们手机的 Wi-Fi 出现了随机断连、无法连接的问题，机型覆盖 Galaxy S24 Plus 和 Galaxy Z Fold 7 等。部分 Galaxy A56、Galaxy A36 和 Galaxy A52s 等用户则表示，他们的手机更新后完全无法识别 SIM 卡。同时部分用户透露，他们的手机连接几小时 Wi-Fi 后就会随机断开，或显示连接错误。有人只能连到 2.4GHz Wi-Fi，完全无法连上较快的 5GHz Wi-Fi。此外，部分用户尝试了重置网络设置、取出 SIM 卡以及重启进入安全模式等方法，均无法解决。由于这些网络断连问题是在安装 One UI 9 后立即出现的，因此可以确定问题源于软件故障，而非硬件问题。截至目前，三星暂未回应此事。

articles.title: 英伟达庆祝首款支持 CUDA 显卡 GeForce 8800 GTX 诞生 20 周年，同步推出纪念游戏带 PC 玩家重返 2006 年
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，英伟达官方今日庆祝 GeForce 8800 GTX 显卡诞生 20 周年，同步推出一款 Steam 演示游戏，带领 PC 玩家回到 2006 年，一睹这款经典显卡的外貌。据IT之家了解，GeForce 8800 GTX 诞生于 2006 年 11 月 8 日，是首款支持 CUDA 的 NVIDIA 显卡，为图形渲染以外的 GPU 计算奠定了基础，并推动形成了加速计算平台。GeForce 8800 GTX 是 06 年的 NVIDIA 旗舰显卡，建议零售价 599 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 4,005 元人民币），采用 Tesla GPU 架构，基于 G80 芯片打造，制程工艺为 90nm，带有 128 个核心。而 CUDA 最初作为并行计算平台和 API 推出，让 GPU 不再局限于图形渲染任务，这套框架成为现代 GPU 架构发展的重要基础。同时，GeForce 8800 GTX 运行频率为 576MHz，配备 768MB GDDR3 显存，位宽为 384-bit，带宽达到 86GB/s。额定功耗 155W，需要 2 个 6-pin 供电接口，并采用 PCIe 1.0 x16 接口。该产品是当时少数能畅玩《孤岛危机》《生化奇兵》等游戏的显卡。它支持 DX10 和 OpenGL 3.3 API。此外，英伟达此次推出的纪念演示游戏由虚幻引擎艺术家 Dylan Browne 创作，带玩家回到一间 2006 年的游戏房。玩家可以在此拆开 GeForce 8800 GTX 的包装，并将其安装到电脑。该演示支持路径追踪、DLSS 4.5 光线重构、动态多帧生成和 RTX Mega Geometry。参考：Steam 上的 GeForce 8800 GTX - 20 Years of a Legend

articles.title: 被网站“断粮”，Anthropic 首次掏钱买新闻内容授权
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，Anthropic 在美国中期选举前夕，与一家新闻出版机构达成了首份内容授权协议。据《Adweek》援引两名知情人士的消息，Anthropic 此次的合作伙伴是美联社（Associated Press，AP）。根据协议，Claude 聊天机器人可以在美国中期选举之夜实时展示美联社的选举结果数据，并注明信息来源。双方没有披露协议的财务条款及有效期限。IT之家注意到，此前 Anthropic 一直拒绝与新闻出版商达成此类内容授权合作，认为通过网络爬虫抓取出版商内容的行为符合合理使用（Fair Use）原则，在法律上是允许的。相比之下，竞争对手 OpenAI 已经与十多家媒体机构达成类似协议，合作伙伴包括阿克塞尔 · 施普林格集团（Axel Springer）、新闻集团（News Corp.）和《大西洋月刊》（The Atlantic）等。不过，由于无法获取新闻出版商提供的最新内容，Claude 在回答具有时效性的问题时受到很大限制。为了迫使 Anthropic 坐到谈判桌前，一些出版商此前已主动屏蔽该公司的网络爬虫，阻止其抓取网站内容。值得一提的是，美联社也是谷歌和 OpenAI 最早达成内容授权合作的媒体机构。目前，Anthropic 正接近上市。

articles.title: 从“争气弹”到“争气路”中国速度独一无二，新型陆基洲际导弹东风-61 确认列装火箭军
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，今天是我国第一枚近程地地导弹“东风一号”成功发射 66 周年，而“东风”家族升级从未止步。2025 年 9 月 3 日，纪念中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争胜利 80 周年阅兵，战略打击群核导弹方队中，新型陆基洲际导弹东风-61 首次公开亮相。据央视新闻今日报道，如今，东风-61 已列装火箭军。军事评论员邵永灵表示，东风-61 从阅兵公开亮相到常态参训，节奏远快于传统洲际导弹的战斗力生成周期。首先，这说明它亮相前已经完成研制、定型、试装与可靠性验证，技术成熟度高。其次，体现火箭军成熟的装备配套与训练体系。东风-61 与现有指挥、通信、保障链路兼容，依托火箭军长期积累的洲际导弹组训经验，部队接装后能够快速吃透新装备，压缩战斗力生成周期，反映改革之后火箭军“核常兼备、全域慑战”建设成效显著。另外，东风-61 常态参训意味着它进入了野外机动、阵地转换、发射流程等实战化课目训练。我国陆基核反击力量实现迭代补强，机动生存、突防打击能力得到充实。报道还提到，从 1960 年“东风一号”腾飞，到如今“东风快递，使命必达”自信宣言，中国导弹工业用六十余年，走过了从仿制到自主、从近程到洲际、从液体到固体、从单一核威慑到核常兼备的跨越式发展之路，已形成覆盖近程、中程、远程、洲际的全射程体系，为国家安全筑起了坚不可摧的钢铁长城。IT之家查询获悉，东风-61 陆基洲际导弹是中国研发的陆基洲际导弹，是维护国家主权、捍卫民族尊严的战略“王牌”。其采用固体燃料推进发射，可以车载机动发射，具有“小快灵”的特点。值得一提的是，机动发射可以躲避卫星侦察和地面监视，也可以在山区快速发射，有更强的生存能力，可以用于二次战略打击。

articles.title: 首发 399 元：达音科推出 DTC500X 电竞声卡，双 CS43198 旗舰 DAC
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，达音科现已推出 DTC500X 电竞声卡。新品主打复古游戏机外形，配备双 CS43198 旗舰 DAC，拥有 4.4mm 平衡 +3.5mm 单端双耳机接口，首发售价 399 元。据介绍，这款产品外观致敬经典游戏掌机，正面的十字键采用锅仔片按键设计。它不承担设备控制功能，而是作为产品设计中的互动元素。机身为 CNC 铝合金材质，背面带有雕刻吉祥物形象。规格方面，该产品搭载双 CS43198 旗舰 DAC，可对声音链路进行全面优化，配合独立 LDO 供电、独立有源晶振等专业音频架构，其动态范围可达 132dB，信噪比为 128dB。配备 3.5mm 单端和 4.4mm 平衡耳机接口，提供高 / 低两种增益模式。此外，该产品专门针对电竞场景进行优化，兼顾音频输出与麦克风输入需求。3.5mm 耳机接口支持四段式麦克风接口，并兼容线控。IT之家附该产品详细参数如下：

articles.title: DeepSeek Harness：日活跃用户达 154 万、日消耗 Token 约 92 万亿，将建设官方插件市场
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，DeepSeek Harness 官方今晚公布了 DeepSeek Harness 产品与社区的进展，并介绍了面向插件作者的支持计划。8 月 13 日，DeepSeek Harness v0.1 版本上线；9 月 29 日，DeepSeek Harness 桌面端正式发布。截至 11 月 4 日，以使用官方 API 的用户为统计范围，DeepSeek Harness 日活跃用户已达 154 万，日消耗 Token 约 92 万亿。IT之家获悉，DeepSeek Harness 发布至今，第三方插件数量已增至约 3.5 万个，约 60% 的活跃用户制作或安装了至少一款第三方插件。官方表示，将会进一步提升插件 API 的稳定性与兼容性，完善插件安全机制，并建设官方插件市场，让插件作者更方便地上传插件、用户更方便地找到自己所需插件。同时，DeepSeek Harness 也正在筹备面向插件作者的支持计划，通过 Token 激励、技术交流与作品推荐，支持新想法的探索与已有作品的完善。具体的支持方式，将结合社区的实际需求与反馈逐步完善。此外，官方也欢迎创业团队和企业通过 DeepSeek Harness 插件接入产品、服务与专业能力，探索合作可能。

articles.title: 实现翻番！今年前三季度我国氢能产业总投资 287 亿元，同比增长 108%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，今年以来，我国氢能产业快速发展，前三季度氢能产业投资实现翻番。数据显示，今年前三季度我国氢能产业总投资 287 亿元，同比增长 108%，实现翻番。可再生能源制氢新开工项目 10 余个，新增投运产能 10 万吨。截至目前，我国可再生能源制氢项目建成投运年产能累计超过 35 万吨，占全球产能比重超过 50％，在建项目的年产能超过 120 万吨，处于全球领先水平。IT之家附不同区域情况如下：华北地区建成的产能最高，占到全国 45%；其次为东北地区，占全国的 36%；第三是西北地区，占到全国的 15%。目前，我国可再生能源制氢中，单体项目规模水平快速提高，万吨以上项目占比接近五成。

articles.title: 摩托罗拉推出 Moto Watch 2 Fit 手表、Moto Buds 2 Ultra 耳机，售价 119 欧元起
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，摩托罗拉今日宣布推出智能穿戴新品，包含 Moto Watch 2 Fit 手表和 Moto Buds 2 Ultra 耳机。售价分别为 119 欧元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 892.8 元人民币）/199 欧元（现汇率约合 1,493 元人民币）。IT之家附两款新品详情如下：Moto Watch 2 Fit这款手表正面配备一块 1.85 英寸 OLED 屏幕，支持 60Hz 刷新率，分辨率为 390 × 450，峰值亮度 1500nits。运行 RTOS 操作系统，内置 400mAh 电池，开启 AOD 情况下续航可达 7 天。同时，该手表提供跑步指数功能，可评估用户的有氧运动能力和跑步效率，并具备睡眠阶段分析、呼吸训练、卡路里分析等功能，支持心率、血氧饱和度、月经周期追踪和压力监测功能，并配备双频 L1/L5 GPS。Moto Buds 2 Ultra这款耳机搭载 Bose SoundDesign 调音技术和 Bose QuietControl 主动降噪技术，拥有 11mm 动圈单元和 Knowles 楼氏动铁单元，支持 Hi-Res Audio、杜比全景声和杜比头部追踪。搭载蓝牙 6.0，支持 SBC、AAC、LHDC 4 和 LHDC 5 音频编码器。每只耳机内置三枚麦克风和一个语音拾取单元。这款耳机单次充电续航最长可达 8 小时，搭配充电盒使用时总续航最长可达 37 小时。充电盒具备 Qi2，支持 AI 实时翻译等功能。

articles.title: 欧洲多架客机遭炸弹威胁，部分已安全降落
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，央视新闻今日报道，欧洲方面消息称，当天欧洲多架客机遭炸弹威胁，涉及一架从爱尔兰都柏林飞往意大利罗马的航班、一架从芬兰赫尔辛基飞往罗马的航班、三架飞往保加利亚索非亚的航班、两架从意大利米兰飞往罗马的航班，其中部分客机已安全降落。图源：Pixabay据法国方面消息，一架从爱尔兰都柏林飞往意大利罗马的空客 A320 客机收到炸弹威胁警报，改道飞往法国，随后安全降落在埃夫勒空军基地。据涉事的爱尔兰航空公司消息，机上共有 151 名乘客和 6 名机组人员，均已被转移至安全区域，排爆人员已抵达现场。保加利亚交通部向当地媒体证实，当天上午 3 架飞往该国索非亚的瑞安航空公司航班遭炸弹威胁，其中从丹麦哥本哈根和西班牙马德里起飞的 2 架已抵达，另一架从伦敦起飞的飞机紧急改道飞往保加利亚普罗夫迪夫。据波兰方面消息，波兰航空公司一架当天计划从华沙飞往巴黎的客机因机上可能存在危险物品的警报，在滑行过程中被叫停。经检查，未发现危险物品，更换飞机后将继续执飞该航班。据意大利方面消息，当天一架从意大利米兰飞往波兰华沙的威兹航空公司客机在捷克上空接到炸弹威胁警报，随后改道飞往奥地利维也纳。航空公司表示正配合有关部门开展调查，目前尚无机上发现爆炸装置的报告。此外，还有一架从芬兰赫尔辛基飞往罗马的航班也收到了炸弹威胁警报，随后被意大利空军护送至罗马安全降落。据比利时方面消息，一架从波兰华沙飞往比利时布鲁塞尔的客机当天因可疑安全报告接受检查，飞机已安全降落在布鲁塞尔机场。IT之家注意到，捷克警方在社交媒体上说，4 架飞往捷克布拉格的客机遭遇炸弹威胁，警方与机场方面随后为飞机降落做准备。3 日，波兰、西班牙、保加利亚和意大利相继报告客机收到炸弹威胁，涉及 7 架客机，部分航班改降、机场短暂关闭。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，苹果全新 MacBook Pro 已正式发布，新机最大的变化莫过于首次将触控屏引入 Mac 产品线，同时采用全新的双层串联 OLED 显示技术，并带来了灵动岛、发光 logo、M5 Pro 和 M5 Max 芯片等一系列升级。这次IT之家拿到的是 16 英寸银色版本 MacBook Pro，具体配置为 M5 Max（18 核 CPU、32 核 GPU）、36GB 统一内存和 2TB 存储空间。相比此前的 MacBook Pro，新机在屏幕、交互方式上都有不少变化，下面一起来看看实拍表现。外观方面，新款 MacBook Pro 延续了苹果熟悉的设计风格，此次拿到的银色版本依旧采用简洁的金属机身，整体观感比较干净利落。值得一提的是，新机背面还重新带回了经典的发光苹果 Logo。距离这一标志性设计退出 MacBook 产品线已有 10 年，如今再次回归，也为新机增添了几分熟悉的味道。另外，新机在保留 16 英寸大屏的同时，进一步减轻了机身重量。具体来看，16 英寸版本重量约为 1.82 千克，相比前代减轻约 320 克，机身厚度也降低近 1 毫米。屏幕是这代 MacBook Pro 最值得关注的升级。新机配备一块 16.3 英寸 PROLED XDR 显示屏，首次采用双层串联 OLED 技术，通过两个自发光像素层实现更高的亮度和对比度。参数方面，这块屏幕 HDR 和 SDR 峰值亮度最高均可达 2000 尼特，对比度达到 10000000:1，支持最高 120Hz ProMotion 自适应刷新率，最低可降至 10Hz。色彩方面则覆盖 P3 和 Adobe RGB 广色域，并经过出厂校准，可满足摄影、视频剪辑、平面设计等专业创作场景的需求。屏幕还配备抗反射涂层，用户也可以选配纳米纹理玻璃，以进一步减少强光环境下的反光和眩光。除了显示效果，这块屏幕还有一个很大的不同：它终于支持触控了。新款 MacBook Pro 首次将触控体验带到 Mac 上，用户可以直接在屏幕上滚动浏览网页、捏合缩放图片，也可以拖动幻灯片、调整窗口位置。对于绘图、视频剪辑和 3D 建模等专业工作，直接在屏幕上进行操作也提供了更多可能。苹果还针对触控操作重新设计了铰链结构，让用户点按屏幕时机身能够保持更加稳定的状态。与此同时，灵动岛也正式登陆 Mac，用户可以通过它查看来电、音乐播放状态和实时活动等信息，并直接进行交互。性能方面，IT之家拿到的这台机器搭载 M5 Max 芯片，拥有 18 核 CPU 和 32 核 GPU，配备 36GB 统一内存及 2TB 存储空间。新款 MacBook Pro 还提供 M5 Pro 版本，最高可选配 128GB 统一内存和 16TB 存储空间。苹果此次还重新设计了整机散热架构，在机身进一步轻薄的同时，兼顾 M5 Pro 和 M5 Max 芯片的持续性能释放。对于需要长时间进行视频渲染、3D 制作和 AI 运算的专业用户来说，这部分升级同样值得关注。其他配置方面，新款 MacBook Pro 配备 1200 万像素 Center Stage 摄像头、录音棚级麦克风，以及全新的六扬声器系统。低音单元经过重新设计，低音下潜能力相比前代增强 50%，同时支持杜比全景声空间音频。接口方面，新机配备 3 个雷雳 5 接口、1 个 HDMI 接口、1 个 SDXC 卡插槽、1 个 MagSafe 磁吸充电接口以及 1 个 3.5mm 耳机插孔，无线连接支持 Wi-Fi 7 和蓝牙 6，并配备 Touch ID 指纹识别。M5 Max 版本最多支持连接 4 台外接显示器。续航方面，苹果官方称新款 MacBook Pro 电池续航时间最长可达 24 小时，并支持快速充电，30 分钟即可充至最高 50%。系统则搭载 macOS 27，针对新加入的触控交互进行了适配，同时支持更多第三方应用调用触控能力。新款 MacBook Pro 已于 10 月 30 日开启预购，将于 11 月 6 日正式发售。以上就是本次IT之家带来的 16 英寸银色版 MacBook Pro 实拍图赏，对于苹果首款触控屏 MacBook 你有何看法？欢迎大家评论分享。IT之家上手视频： 京东 Apple MacBook Pro (PROLED XDR 显示屏) M5 Pro 14 寸 (15+16 核) 24G 1T 深空黑色触摸屏笔记本电脑 21499 元直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: NASA 公布 X-70 Fractal 实验飞机：探索极限机动能力，两年内首飞
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，NASA 昨日宣布，X 系列实验飞机家族迎来新成员 ——X-70 Fractal。该系列此前诞生过近 80 年前首次突破音障的贝尔 X-1，以及近年来备受关注的 X-59 静音超音速验证机。NASA 表示，X-70 Fractal 是一个“高性能、高适应性的研究平台”，将作为新一代航空技术的试验平台，用于相关技术的开发与测试。目前，NASA 仅公布了一张由人工智能生成的 X-70 效果图，飞机主体笼罩在烟雾和阴影之中。不过，该机构已经确认了这款飞机的多项性能指标。X-70 将采用有人驾驶设计，巡航速度为 0.75 马赫，最高飞行高度可达 4.5 万英尺（IT之家注：约 13,716 米），作战任务航程超过 1,726 英里（约 2,778 公里）。在载荷方面，X-70 最多可搭载 2,000 磅（约 907.2 千克）的实验设备，这些设备既可以安装在机身内部，也可以挂载在机身外部。此外，X-70 还将配备先进的飞行控制技术，能够快速重新配置飞行控制系统。NASA 希望借此探索有人驾驶飞机此前从未展示过的机动能力。NASA 局长贾里德 · 艾萨克曼（Jared Isaacman）表示：“X-70 Fractal 为 NASA 提供了一个高性能有人驾驶平台，可以在真实飞行环境中测试先进的飞行控制技术、机动能力以及其他前沿技术。”他还表示，X-70 采用模块化设计，能够快速更换机身内部和外部的任务载荷。这种设计可以让科研团队持续开展飞行测试、积累数据，并迅速从一项实验转向下一项实验。NASA 预计，X-70 将在未来两年内以 NASA 名义完成首次飞行。艾萨克曼表示，X-70 只是 NASA 航空研究新阶段的一部分。

articles.title: 云存储服务提供商 Dropbox 计划收购 Tigris Data，拓展企业开发者 AI 存储服务
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，云存储服务提供商 Dropbox 今日宣布计划收购分布式对象存储平台 Tigris Data，加速拓展面向企业开发者的 AI 基础设施服务。IT之家了解到，Dropbox 今日还推出了 DBX Agent Cloud 服务，初期提供对象存储功能。该公司还将对核心产品进行重大升级，将 AI 直接引入客户现有工作流程。Dropbox 计划将自身技术扩展至 AI 应用开发企业，并为现有客户提供全新 AI 功能。他们可以让 Dropbox 直接处理现有文件中的指定任务，也可以在受支持的第三方 AI 工具中调用 Dropbox 内容，还能自主选择 AI 模型，同时保留原有的文件权限、历史记录和协作上下文。此外，Dropbox 计划在未来推出 DBX Agent Cloud，为开发 AI 应用和智能体的企业及开发者提供存储与数据基础设施服务。该服务初期将提供独立的、兼容 S3 协议的对象存储产品。企业可以单独购买，并通过熟悉的工具以及为 Amazon S3 构建的兼容应用使用这项服务。

articles.title: 91% ≈ 0%？谷歌最新研究，戳破工程 Agent 的高正确率泡沫
articles.content: 41.3% 的设计项跨过安全门槛，复杂工程仍困于约束耦合。    作者丨郑佳美 岑   峰    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       在工程世界里，91% 的正确，有时和 0% 的交付能力没有区别。一条电缆桥架在机房顶部穿过消防管线，就能让几十页正确的计算书失去交付价值。载流量算对了，电压降符合要求，设备选型也有依据，但进入三维空间后，几套系统争夺同一段净空，工程师只能退回方案。AI Agent 能快速完成局部计算，工程项目却不会按计算题的边界运转：一处调整牵动另一处，刚核验过的结果也可能随修订失效。Google 与 Mercor 近日发布的 Physical-Engineering's Last Exam（PLE），以 85 项机械、电气、土木与结构工程任务量化了这种落差。在 56 项隐藏测试中，Claude Opus 5.5 搭配 Claude Code 得分 48.3%，而在共同创作任务中，它平均满足 91% 的单项约束，只有 41.3% 的交付设计项满足全部硬性安全与可行性要求。更棘手的是，剩下的 9% 往往无法靠继续提高模型的计算能力解决。因为工程设计中的要求彼此关联，解决一个问题，可能又会产生新的问题。PLE 的技术设计恰好揭示了这一困境：当局部能力已经足够强，工程 Agent 究竟还缺少什么？01工程 Agent 正在遭遇可行域瓶颈此前很多 Agent 评测采用逐项累积分数的方式，只要完成更多要求，就能取得更高评价。这适合衡量知识理解和单点执行能力，却会掩盖工程设计中的一类关键失败：模型可能满足了绝大多数要求，但剩下一条恰好决定方案能否投入使用。PLE 在 41 项人机共同创作任务中，将工程约束与设计优化放进同一套评价体系。其中 37 项采用约束评分，在统一评分机制下，40% 的评分空间取决于单项检查通过比例，另外 60% 则与成本或性能优化有关。不过，优化部分存在一个前提：全部硬性安全与可行性约束必须通过。研究团队将其称为硬约束门控（Hard-Constraint Gating）。这个机制有一处关键设计。即使某个方案能够显著降低材料费用，只要违反了一项硬约束，就无法获得成本优化部分的分数。系统仍然记录它已经完成的检查，但不会允许经济收益抵消工程缺陷。PLE 同时设置了合规但未经充分优化的基线方案，以及合规成本的下界。前者用于判断 Agent 是否产生了实际优化收益，后者则为成本改善提供衡量尺度。这样，模型既不能通过选用过量设备轻松满足规范，也无法靠牺牲可行性获得漂亮的成本数字。这种评分方式让一个长期存在的问题变得清晰：工程设计中的优化空间受到约束限制，并且约束之间往往存在联系。例如，在冷却系统设计中，管径决定水力阻力，水力阻力影响水泵工作点，而实际流量又决定换热能力。Agent 如果只根据材料成本缩小管径，后续可能需要更高扬程的水泵，原本节省的费用反而转移到设备和运行能耗上。工程上把所有约束同时成立的设计范围称为可行域。它包含连续变化的参数，也受到设备型号、标准尺寸等离散条件限制。模型每修改一个变量，其他参数能够选择的范围便可能发生变化。这给 Agent 带来一种与普通推理不同的要求。生成候选方案之后，还需要判断当前哪些条件已经接近允许边界，以及下一次修改会影响哪些约束。工程优化中，这些限制进一步调整空间的条件通常被称为活跃约束。PLE 没有直接为 Agent 提供可行域搜索算法，但硬约束门控让这种能力缺口可以被测量。91% 的单项约束满足比例说明，模型已经能够处理大部分局部要求，剩余困难集中在多个条件共同成立，以及满足条件后继续优化。而当设计从单次求解进入长时间、多轮修改时，问题还会继续扩大：此前满足的约束，未必在下一轮操作后仍然有效。02长流程能力正在变成状态一致性问题PLE 的任务环境没有将设计条件整理成一份完整说明。85 项任务累计包含 51

articles.title: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05390v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. Yet a reviewer can both repair errors and replace decisions that were already correct. We study this as a problem of institutional jurisdiction: conditional on the same proposal, task information, model, and review output, when is the reviewer authorized to make its recommendation binding? We compare broad override authority with an evidence gate that permits replacement only after the reviewer produces a mechanically valid record of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. Across two locally run open-weight models, 96 spatial-policy tasks, and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark, the gate sharply reduces corruption of correct proposals while retaining most repairs of violations. articles.title: Agent Harness Awareness: Turning Verified Telemetry into Operational Control for Tool-Using Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05391v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tool descriptions tell an agent what an action can do, but they do not necessarily reveal whether that action is healthy or suitable at the moment of use. Execution harnesses often possess this information through monitors, traces, and recent failures while the model choosing the next action does not. We call this gap operational blindness. We introduce Agent Harness Awareness, a trust-separated design in which the host supplies a small, fresh, verified state snapshot before a consequential action while retaining measurement, enforcement, evaluation, and final dispatch authority. We test its tools-and-network instance with ToolRoute, a controlled isolation benchmark that holds the task and candidate semantics constant and varies the operational information available to the model. In a 216-decision ablation across GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, and Gemini 3.7 Flash, verified tool-health state reduced mean observable policy regret by 96.9%

articles.title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05392v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems powered by large language models (LLMs) execute as autonomous multi-step pipelines that dynamically invoke tools, integrate observations into memory, and iterate until a task is resolved or a resource budget is exhausted. Unlike classical workflows with fixed graphs, the aggregate compute, bandwidth, and end-to-end latency demands of such pipelines are unknown at dispatch time: they emerge at runtime from intermediate observations and stochastic token sampling, yielding heavy-tailed, multi-modal random variables. This unpredictability forces infrastructure orchestrators into a dilemma: under-provisioning risks mid-execution throttling and deadline violations, while over-provisioning wastes scarce edge or cloud capacity. articles.title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05393v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We argue that a key limitation is that existing systems select experts and retrieve knowledge from the question alone, rather than from gaps that emerge during reasoning. These signals trigger targeted knowledge retrieval or mid-discussion specialist recruitment. Abstract: As agents become more capable, they are moving beyond one-off tasks toward sustained assistance across successive user goals. Abstract: We evaluate the extent to which agentic AI models can complete an end-to-end data science project, and how this improves with feedback. A 'writer' model with specific tools creates a complete data science project including downloading, cleaning, and analyzing a dataset, and writing a short paper about it. Of the 147 initial submissions, 107 run and render, and the average score increases from 59 per cent to 76 per cent after the final round of feedback. articles.content:

Abstract: Transparency has become a central principle in AI governance, yet there is little agreement about what transparency means, for whom, and in what contexts. articles.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05556v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-as-a-judge is a common substitute for costly human evaluation, and aggregating several judges is the standard remedy for any single judge's bias. Judge pools mix judges of very different reliability, while the human-labeled sets that validate them hold a few hundred items or fewer. In this regime the per-item mean weights weak judges as heavily as strong ones, and confusion-table models such as Dawid-Skene must estimate a per-judge error table from too few items. We propose AGORA (Aggregation Of Reliability-weighted Assessments), an item-response-theory aggregator that places every item on one latent quality scale and describes each judge by a sensitivity parameter and ordered rating thresholds, so judge reliability is learned from all items jointly and without human labels. Abstract: Real-world vision is dynamic and scene-rich, while EEG and fMRI resolve it at complementary temporal and spatial scales. Most neural decoding systems, however, align one modality in isolation and mostly against static images or short clips. Abstract: As autonomous AI agents enter permissionless onchain markets, selecting new service providers remains a core challenge. Abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) speeds up large language model (LLM) serving, but its gain depends on the workload's \emph{shape}, such as batch size and context length, and on its \emph{content}. A model-based drafter proposes a short block on any content, while a model-free drafter such as n-gram lookup proposes long copies at almost no cost when the output repeats its input, as in code editing. Adaptive verification spends a batch-wide verification budget on the draft tokens most likely to be accepted, but it supports only one model-based drafter. Abstract: On Replit, our agentic engineering platform, users now build entire products without writing code, through successive feature requests to an agent. Yet existing coding benchmarks evaluate single, fully specified tasks, and many are near saturation. Abstract: Spectral graph generation models graphs through the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of their Laplacians, providing a compact and continuous alternative to direct graph construction. However, these eigensystems must retain the structural properties of graph Laplacians. Existing approaches preserve eigenvector orthonormality but do not enforce the Laplacian nullspace constraint, potentially producing eigensystems inconsistent with Laplacian structure. To address this, we introduce Laplacian-Constrained Stiefel Flow Matching (LaSFM), which preserves the nullspace condition alongside eigenvector orthonormality and positive eigenvalues during generation. We characterize the underlying constrained Stiefel manifold and formulate flow matching on it. We further extend LaSFM to property-guided generation, steering samples toward desired graph properties while maintaining these constraints. Abstract: High-fidelity simulation of dynamical systems is central to scientific discovery and engineering design, yet remains computationally demanding. articles.title: Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning for Multi-Objective Alignment
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05506v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with several objectives, such as helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty, typically relies on preference judgment for each objective, growing the annotation cost linearly with the number of objectives. Active preference learning can reduce this cost by selecting the comparisons whose labels are expected to change the policy most. Existing remedies either lack an objective-aware query selection mechanism for the multi-objective setting or regard conflicting preferences as harmful, therefore excluding them from the training data. We introduce OGC-DPO (Objective-conditioned Gradient Coverage DPO), an active learning framework that treats each (response pair, objective) combination as a separate query and measures its informativeness through the policy's own implicit gradient, without relying on an external reward model. OGC-DPO then selects the queries that most expand each objective's gradient coverage.

Abstract: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) eliminates the central aggregation server but remains vulnerable to data heterogeneity, Byzantine attacks, and channel noise. We show that noise accumulates as models propagate across nodes, becoming increasingly significant as the learning rate decays. Abstract: Support vector machines (SVMs) are fundamentally grounded in geometric margin maximisation and currently lack a mainstream probabilistic interpretation. We further show that this same divergence formulation recovers the exact objective function for kernel ridge regression when domain constraints are removed and $L^2$ regularisation is applied. articles.title: Exploring the Privacy--Size Tradeoff for Differentially Private Self-Attentive Variational Autoencoders
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05582v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Data tends to be most useful when it is shared, and the data most worth sharing is often the data that privacy obligations restrict. Synthetic data from a generator trained under differential privacy (DP) is one way to reconcile the two, but its utility depends on the privacy budget $\varepsilon$ and on how much data the generator sees - a parameter that most data sharing applications of synthetic data control. We present SAVANT, a self-attentive variational autoencoder for tabular data trained with DP-SGD that, to our knowledge, is the first to combine attention, a VAE, and DP in one tabular model. We evaluate it against two marginal mechanisms, PrivBayes and MST, jointly over the privacy budget and the dataset size on two public datasets, measuring the utility a downstream classifier loses by training on synthetic rather than real data. We find that, under the same DP guarantee, more data generally means more utility. For the marginal

articles.title: C-GRPO: Conformal Group Relative Policy Optimization
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05591v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning-oriented language model training increasingly relies on multiple on-policy rollouts, but standard Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) uses a fixed group size, wasting compute on easy prompts and under-exploring hard ones. Existing adaptive-budget methods alleviate this inefficiency, yet their stopping rules are heuristic and do not provide a finite-sample calibration guarantee. We propose CGRPO, which replaces the fixed rollout budget of standard GPRO with calibrated conformal thresholds over task-specific nonconformity scores, combining Adaptive Prediction Set (APS)-style calibration for closed-form reasoning, a first-success score for execution-based code, automatic miscoverage selection, and periodic re-calibration. We prove finite-sample coverage for the resulting stopping rule and show that, under monotone policy improvement, recalibration induces a non-increasing expected training budget. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05594v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Relevance propagation, which redistributes a network's prediction backward through the layers, is usually treated as a heuristic. We show that it is the solution of a single variational problem: Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) is the divergence-free flow on the active computational graph of zero relative entropy to the backward transition law of the forward activation flow; for a non-negative reference, this is a relative entropy between Markov measures on backward paths. The rules LRP$_0$, LRP$_{z^+}$ and LRP$_{\alpha,\beta}$ follow from this principle by the choice of a reference, and are instances of one rule, LRPN$_{\alpha,\beta}$, whose weights may vary from node to node, for instance with the node's activity, in the spirit of Hebb's principle. articles.title: RIDGE: State-Conditioned Reward Blending for Behavioral Coverage in Deep RL Game Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05601v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A deep RL agent trained on a fixed persona reward plays one way: an Explorer keeps exploring while starving, a Survivor hoards on an empty map. Since each persona fixes its own reward, automated playtesting trains N agents for N styles. Changing reward composition mid-episode runs into the switching-stability dilemma: PPO degrades under non-stationary rewards. We present RIDGE, a single-agent architecture that sidesteps the dilemma with two design choices: a state-conditioned blender that computes softmax-normalized sigmoid weights from slow-moving state variables, and a multi-head critic that trains one value head per persona on its own stationary signal. articles.title: Transport along Local Annealing Paths: Wasserstein Geometry and Multimodal Sampling
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05605v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Variational approaches to learning transport maps for multimodal sampling can suffer from mode collapse. One way to mitigate this problem is to learn transport along a prescribed path of intermediate distributions defined by geometric annealing. We show that annealing can take a substantial detour in Wasserstein space: when mass moves between modes, the path can be much longer than the distance between its endpoints. We further link path geometry to transport learning, showing that long annealing paths can slow population optimization, while sufficiently regular paths permit rapid convergence. Motivated by these findings, we propose componentwise annealed transport (CAT) to reduce the need for mass transfer between modes. Starting from a mode-informed mixture reference, CAT constructs an exact mixture decomposition of the target and learns separate transport maps along componentwise annealing paths. articles.title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05609v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) extends on-policy distillation (OPD) to consolidate capabilities from multiple teachers. Although prior work reports near-perfect in-distribution (IND) distillation performance, we find that this can mask incomplete capability consolidation beyond the supervised distribution. A preliminary study on synthetic reasoning shows that OPD does not fully transfer teachers' generalization capabilities. We then extend this investigation to real-world tasks, evaluating extrapolative and compositional generalization across mathematical reasoning, coding, agent, and long-context capabilities using Qwen3 models. Across extrapolative settings, OPD and MOPD reach 96.04-102.73% of their teachers' IND scores. Yet their out-of-distribution (OOD) scores remain 2.45-16.25% below the base model's. articles.title: LACS: Distribution-Sensitive Label-Agnostic Confidence Selection for Dynamic Data Pruning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05616v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training on large datasets motivates selecting which examples receive expensive training computation. Fixed quotas determine the amount of pruning in advance, while absolute confidence cutoffs depend on the score scale. We study a population-relative alternative that adapts the threshold and retained count together. We introduce LACS (Label-Agnostic Confidence Selector), a training-time rule based on maximum predictive confidence, requiring neither labels at selection time nor per-example gradients. LACS removes examples at or above a log-mean-exp reference plus a margin. We characterize its sensitivity to score gaps and mass, and derive an exact no-pruning condition. For $0<\rho<1$, the removed fraction is at most $\rho$ and at least one example remains. The unsigned score permits both confidently correct and confidently wrong examples to be removed. articles.title: Data-Efficient Scaling-Law Discovery for Recommendation Systems via Coupled Hyperparameter Scaling
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05643v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large-scale ranking and recommendation models of Web platforms benefit from increased compute much as large language models do, and their scaling behavior is broadly power-law in form. Yet ranking models have heterogeneous architectures which makes their scaling law less straightforward than that of LLMs. We address how to discover the scaling law of an arbitrary ranking model efficiently. We introduce a scaling layer, which groups primitive architecture parameters into semantically coherent groups and defines how they co-vary, inducing a mapping from a low-dimensional space of hyper-hyperparameters into the full architecture space. On top of it, Axia fits scaling-informed surrogates, selects configurations by a posterior-based acquisition criterion, and returns a Pareto frontier from which per-model operating points are validated -- replacing exhaustive sweeps with a small number of informative runs. Abstract: Comparing sparse autoencoders (SAEs) requires connecting feature correspondence, differences between whole dictionaries, and uncertainty from finite evaluation data. We develop a framework that connects these tasks through an energy-weighted optimal-transport plan under a specified similarity geometry. The same plan defines a dictionary-level discrepancy, decomposes it into latent contributions, and quantifies how each latent's mass is distributed across counterparts. We characterize relationships between decoder, activation, and first-order causal similarities; idealized models clarify the interpretation of splitting and absorption. For fixed trained SAEs, we derive joint asymptotic inference for transport costs and fractions, accounting for activation similarities and both energy marginals estimated from the same documents. articles.title: Beyond Accuracy: Information-Theoretic Decoder Evaluation Under Latent Intent
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05658v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A central challenge in assistive brain-to-robot control is decoding a user's latent intent from complex and noisy brain signals. Prior approaches evaluate decoders as single-trial classifiers with accuracy-based metrics, but this neglects the inherently sequential nature of assistive control. Since a planner must integrate intermittent, noisy decoder outputs over time, single-step accuracy can only be a proxy when predicting downstream task performance. We formalize brain-to-robot control as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), and prove that there is a sharp phase transition: regret is uniformly bounded across the horizon as long as pairs of goals are all decoder-distinguishable, but grows linearly otherwise. We show that a single channel statistic, the worst-pair Chernoff information $\Gamma_{\min}$ sets this boundary. articles.title: Discourse Analysis of Legislative Bill Discussions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05381v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Legislative hearings are distinct communication events with their own human recognizable structure and logic, yet they have been analyzed as distinct phenomena beyond their transcripts. Understanding legislative hearings at a deeper level is a major step in analyzing the work and power relationships within democratic bodies. In this work, we present a novel end-to-end pipeline for parsing rhetorical structures from legislative committee hearings with the goal of improving legislative discourse analysis and democratic accountability. We also propose a rhetorical structure grammar and find that 55.21% of California state bill discussions in our dataset can be parsed with this grammar. We evaluate our pipeline with two utterance section classifiers on a random subset of over 2,000 annotated utterances corresponding to 100 hearings. articles.title: DS@GT ARC at CheckThat! 2026: A Verdict-Anchored Pipeline for Generating Fact-Checking Articles
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05382v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Misinformation spreads faster than professional fact-checkers can manually verify it and write articles explaining their verdicts. This creates a need to automate the production of fact-checking articles. This paper details work done by the DS@GT ARC team for CLEF 2026 CheckThat! Lab Task 3 Fact-Checking Article Generation. We seek to generate a full fact-checking article from a claim, its original verdict, and a set of scraped source documents. Our team built a four-stage pipeline that cleans noisy evidence, retrieves and clusters relevant sources, generates the article by conditioning \texttt{Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct} on the original fact-checker verdict, and recovers inline citations through deterministic post-processing. We achieved a mean score of 0.428 and ranked 3rd out of 9 teams for the CLEF 2026 CheckThat! Lab Task 3, compared to a baseline mean score of 0.272. Our code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/dsgt-arc/checkth

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05383v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) demands more than empathic validation, requiring instead a structured formulation of the interplay among situations, automatic thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. Therapists formalize this interplay through a Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram, where maintaining longitudinal coherence necessitates continuous evidential adjudication to separate tentative hypotheses from established findings. Consequently, provisional interpretations are often prematurely reified as established facts, inadvertently biasing downstream interventions. articles.title: Human-like cross-language generalisation in deep neural speaker embeddings and its acoustic foundations
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05384v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generalisability is a central question for deep neural networks, including the cross-language generalisation of speaker embeddings. This study examined whether deep neural speaker embeddings generalise across languages and how such generalisation relates to human perception and acoustic structure. Using Cantonese--English bilingual speech presented in within- and cross-language conditions, we derived similarity from 18 state-of-the-art models and compared it with human ratings and acoustic features using linear mixed models and representational similarity analysis. Embeddings exhibited cross-language generalisation that broadly paralleled human behaviour, reflecting accurate identity discrimination and sensitivity to language switching. This generalisation relied on largely shared acoustic cues with language-sensitive weighting, mirroring human patterns. articles.title: Same Origin, Different Verdicts: Text Production Conditions Confound Machine-Generated Text Detection in Russian
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05385v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated detection of machine-generated text is applied where the verdict carries a cost for the author, yet origin is a property of the production process, not an observable property of the text. The conditions under which a text is produced push it in the same direction in which a generative model is presumed to push it. This study measures the contribution of these conditions while origin is held fixed. The Russian-language corpus of 1882 documents comprises a machine part, generated by four generation channels (each backed by its own model family) across 45 tasks in three task modes, and an archival human part annotated for source regimentation level before the texts were read. The primary contrast is computed within the machine corpus: both halves of a pair are generated by the same model for the same task and differ only in task wording. articles.title: SRRM: A Retrieval-Reconstruction Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Context Memory in Small Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05386v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Small Language Models (SLMs) are increasingly deployed on consumer-grade hardware, yet their ability to preserve information across progressively longer contexts remains insufficiently understood. Existing benchmarks primarily evaluate retrieval-oriented tasks, providing limited insight into whether successful retrieval reflects comprehensive long-context memory preservation. To address this limitation, this paper introduces Simple Retrieval-Reconstruction Memory (SRRM), a lightweight and fully reproducible benchmark that jointly evaluates Targeted Retrieval and Global Information Reconstruction. This study also proposes the Memory Preservation Ratio (MPR), a benchmark-level metric that quantifies the relationship between retrieval and reconstruction performance. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05389v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative AI is currently fragmented, with separate subscriptions required for text generation, image synthesis, and code assistance, leading to high costs and workflow disruptions. AI Express is a SaaS platform that consolidates these capabilities into a unified pay-as-you-go service. The platform provides a range of AI tools, including a Core Code Reviewer that evaluates GitHub repositories, a Text-to-Website generator that converts text into fully functional websites, script generation, grammar checking, data analysis, and watermark removal, all accessible through a single interface without requiring technical expertise.

articles.title: When to Ask, When to Answer: Strategic Clarification for Ambiguous Reference Resolution in Dialogue
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05517v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For humans, referential disambiguation is a collaborative process involving clarification questions asked when they will meaningfully change the outcome. However, large language models (LLMs) have been shown to be biased toward premature answering, preferring definite single-turn responses over more clarification exchanges. In this paper, we study the problem of "strategic clarification" -- asking clarification questions in a reference game when their answers will narrow the set of candidate referents. We construct a controlled test environment from the SIMMC 2.1 dataset that records how many questions each ambiguous reference needs to be successfully resolved, and examine how baseline LLM behavior and common post-training methods ask clarifying questions vs. attempt to answer the referent. articles.title: Rewrite, Then Veto: Rewriter-Agnostic Edit Gating for LLM-Based Post-OCR Correction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05539v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLMs can repair noisy OCR transcripts of historical documents, but they also change text that was already correct. We propose EditVeto, a veto gate placed after a full-context LLM rewrite. The rewrite is character-aligned to the OCR input, its differences are split into blocks, and a 0.6B-parameter gate keeps or reverts each block. An oracle analysis motivates the design: given the true error locations, per-span generation is worse than no correction, whereas vetoing a full rewrite's edits helps. Trained on rewrites by two Qwen3 models and evaluated, frozen, on the eight HIPE-OCRepair-2026 test sets, the gate improves all five rewriters tested, two of them unseen in training: weighted cMER falls by 0.0026-0.0044 and the preference score rises by 0.15-0.25 (paired bootstrap, p ~ 0.0002 each). articles.title: RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05596v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Different retrievers exist for retrieval-augmented generation, yet none performs best for all queries. Therefore, the key question is: given a query and retrieved passages from different retrievers, which one is most suited for that query? Existing routers usually make predictions from query-specific features and a fixed pool of retrievers; such routers have no output for an unseen retriever and are incapable by design on a new corpus. To fill these gaps, RAGCompass reads the retrieved passage sets themselves: passages from an unfamiliar retriever or corpus stay directly comparable to other passages, so routing stays well designed where a query-only map would fail. We contrastively fine-tune a reranker against the answer each evidence set produces, which accounts for most of the gain; a small comparison head adds a moderate improvement, and neither component has retriever-specific parameters. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05637v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech transcription errors can be difficult to recognize when competing word hypotheses are unfamiliar or visually similar. We describe an interface that combines alternative transcripts, replay and contextually checked pictograms for selected uncertain concepts. The system will initially support French and Spanish functional utterances. A counterbalanced study will assess whether pictorial feedback helps listeners recover the speaker's intended action beyond text alternatives alone. We will also quantify semantic mismatch and additional interaction time, since an inappropriate image can reinforce the wrong interpretation rather than repair it.

articles.content:

Abstract: Search can help LLM agents correct mistakes, but their starting conditions may shape which evidence they find and use. Drawing on cognitive-bias paradigms, we develop a controlled search harness to examine result order, records of prior work, and initial hypotheses while holding each question and document collection fixed. Matched controls distinguish order effects from differences in document composition and the effects of failed work from context length. Across 10 models and 1,000 synthetic search worlds, we track queries, retrieved documents, document openings, and final answers. articles.title: Prospective Memory for Proactive LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most memory systems for LLM agents are retrospective, preserving and retrieving past information to inform current decisions. Proactive agents, however, also require prospective memory: retaining future-directed intentions and realizing them when appropriate opportunities arise, even without explicit requests. Crucially, remembering the right intention does not guarantee acting at the right time: a related observation may call for waiting, while a later cue may make the same intention actionable. Inspired by cognitive theories of human prospective memory, we introduce Pro-Memory, a memory framework that separates maintaining future intentions from deciding when and how to realize them. Pro-Memory preserves pending objectives linked to their supporting evidence, assesses new observations against their original goals and activation conditions, and coordinates appropriate contributions with the agent's ongoing actions. Abstract: This study investigates the authorship impersonation capacity of six widely used large language models (LLMs): Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Opus, GPT 5.2, GPT 5.2 Pro, DeepSeek 3.2, and Grok 4.1 Fast. The evaluation was conducted using short product review texts selected to ensure high within author consistency in individual writing style. Authorship mimicry was evaluated using a cosine distance based distance to training metric, supplemented by visual analyses of embedding distributions. articles.title: Phonological Knowledge of Chinese Characters in Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05803v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: How much phonological knowledge do language models (LMs) possess about Chinese characters, and how is this knowledge represented and used? We introduce PinyinBench, a controlled benchmark covering homophones, phonological features (initials, finals, and tones), and polyphonic characters. We investigate 17 text-only and multimodal LMs through three complementary approaches: behavioral evaluation, layer-wise probing, and activation steering. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05814v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models increasingly automate complex tasks, but human decision capacity does not scale with their capabilities. In many applications, humans remain essential for providing private context, authority, or judgments unavailable to the agent. We formulate human decision capacity allocation: given multiple consultation opportunities and a limited budget, at which decisions should an LLM agent consult a human? The central challenge is estimating consultation value, which is executor-dependent because the same human input may benefit different downstream agents differently. We introduce Consultation Value Distillation (CVD), which estimates consultation values offline using Monte Carlo executor rollouts and distills these values into lightweight predictors for budgeted allocation, requiring no rollout-based value estimation at deployment. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05827v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Decision models choose among predefined options in tasks such as routing and action selection. In multi-agent collaboration, a decision determines how members divide work, exchange resources, and act in parallel. We introduce TandemBench, a benchmark of 1,200 questions in multi-agent cooking scenarios where coordination choices affect goal completion. Models receive complete global information and candidate team plans, with reference answers established through execution and exact search. Models select an optimal team plan and, in paired variants that retain or remove it, judge whether better arrangements exist beyond the supplied options. We evaluate 40 native decision models and compare them with 10 general-purpose language models. The best native decision model achieves 62.50% decision accuracy. Abstract: Large language model (LLM) shopping assistants now recommend products in multi-turn conversations. However, reliable evaluation faces Data scarcity and Difficulty Standardizing Criteria. To address these obstacles, we introduce CARTBench for CART (Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines). For Difficulty Standardizing Criteria, we develop case-specific rubrics guided by Ideal Response Principles, distilled from excellent replies manually selected from successfully completed orders. These principles also guide Principle-Guided CART Prompting, our structured recommendation strategy. Abstract: Confidence estimates guide human review in LLM-built knowledge graphs, but better error prediction can yield little improvement in an audit. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05380v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual autoregressive generation spans two dominant paradigms: next-scale prediction for images and video, and next-frame prediction for video. Both decode block-by-block rather than token-by-token, yielding KV caches whose statistics diverge from those of language models. At scale, KV memory exceeds the weights and limits large-scale deployment caused by a large amount of visual tokens. Our analysis of these caches reveals three findings. First, a small set of massive-value channels carries the functional load: ablating these outlier channels collapses generation, whereas ablating a matched set of inlier channels leaves quality intact. Second, the outliers organize along two axes, feature and block, with magnitudes persistent within each cell and shifting across cells. Abstract: In Bangladesh, much localized misinformation spreads as photocards: single-image news summaries that imitate the branding of well-known news organizations. Sixteen photometric and morphological transformations per image grow the corpus to 32,736 samples. articles.content:

Abstract: The hand localization problem has been a longstanding focus due to its many applications. The task involves modeling the hand as a singular point and determining its position within a defined coordinate system. However, due to data modality limitations, existing hand localization technologies face several challenges. For example, vision-based localization raises privacy concerns, while wearable-based methods compromise user comfort. In this paper, we introduce mmHand, a new device-free, privacy-preserving dynamic hand localization system with pixel-level accuracy, using a single commodity mmWave device. We first propose a mmImage generation tool to fully extract spatial information from raw mmWave data and introduce a novel 2D image-format representation of mmWave data. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05406v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Contrastive pretraining has advanced image-text understanding, yet image, video, and audio encoders are still trained independently, with cross-modal alignment realized mainly through post-hoc binding to a frozen anchor space. We present Omni-Encoder, a general multimodal encoder that processes image, video, audio, and audio-visual inputs within a single SigLIP-2 Vision Transformer with fully shared parameters. Unlike anchor-centric binding or per-modality adapters, all modalities are optimized jointly end-to-end, and the framework is organized from input to training. A modality-native input stage first maps each signal into the shared embedding space, including a 1D-convolutional audio tokenizer that converts mel-spectrograms into tokens aligned with visual patches. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05407v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion image generators are successful due to accurate denoising networks and strong numerical samplers. Yet the two components are not fully matched. During sampling, the denoiser predicts for the next step based on flawed input that differ much from the real data. This train-test gap, or exposure bias, caps image generation quality (i.e., blurry, lacking in details or awkward in shape). To mitigate the problem, we propose PEEK, a novel training-free deterministic sampler plugin. At each eligible denoising step, PEEK first performs a provisional one-step update, evaluates the denoiser once at the look-ahead state, and interpolates it with the one-step-later prediction to form the next noisy state. By taking the additional step, we obtain a generally more-image-like prediction from the higher-signal noisy state, mitigating the exposure bias. Abstract: Low-textured sketch images are widely used in scientific applications, including wildlife conservation, archaeological illustration, and forensic composites. Learning from and retrieving such images is challenging because they lack detailed surface textures and visual variations commonly exploited by modern deep learning models. This paper proposes Augmentation with Reinforcement Transformation (ART) to fine-tune pretrained models to learn effective representations for accurate sketch image retrieval. Our key observation is that sketches are particularly sensitive to image transformations, such as rotation, flipping, zooming, and stretching. Abstract: Point cloud denoising aims to recover clean geometry from noisy 3D observations while preserving both fine surface details and the underlying spatial distribution of the points. Many learning-based methods adopt a two-stage pipeline that first extracts point-wise features from the noisy input and subsequently predicts point-wise displacements via simple regressions. However, these approaches often lack robust feature guidance and distribution-aware geometric refinement, causing them to fail at maintaining optimal point uniformity and geometric quality. To address these limitations, we propose PointNDF, a denoising framework that combines patch-level geometric context with local displacement prediction. Abstract: Surgical world models have the potential to provide intra-operative guidance, accelerate risk-free training and facilitate transfer of expert surgical maneuvers. However, the use of world models for transferring surgical expertise has been largely unexplored. Moreover, recent approaches in this domain have mainly relied on ground truth kinematics actions or expert annotations for specific tasks, limiting their applicability beyond the narrow range of tasks with ground-truth annotations. In contrast, existing works in the natural domain have shown promising results in learning latent actions solely from unlabeled videos and transferring the learned actions across contexts. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05449v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Learning on boundary representations (B-reps) requires robustness to the pose of a part, since CAD models are not stored in a canonical orientation. Existing B-rep networks either operate on world-frame coordinates and normals, and thus degrade under rotation, or encode each face in a local reference frame. Local frames yield invariance, but reduce inter-face messages to scalars and discard the relative orientation of adjacent faces. We propose SO3brep, an SO(3)-equivariant graph neural network on the B-rep face-adjacency graph. Node features are computed in local frames and mapped into a shared frame by Wigner D-matrices. Clebsch-Gordan tensor products couple these features with the directions between adjacent faces, so that relative orientation is preserved throughout message passing and the output remains SE(3)-invariant. articles.title: From Tokens to Trajectories: Parameter-Efficient Continuous Adaptation of Unified Multimodal Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05451v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While discrete tokenization in Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) establishes strong semantic reasoning, it introduces a strict quantization bottleneck that degrades fine-grained visual details, often resulting in structurally accurate but artifact-heavy images. We introduce FlowShift, a parameter-efficient post-training framework that bypasses this bottleneck by converting pre-trained discrete UMMs into continuous rectified-flow generators. Instead of discarding the backbone's semantic priors, FlowShift replaces discrete visual interfaces with continuous latent projections and applies LoRA to the attention layers. To efficiently boost visual quality without semantic drift, we propose Dual-Objective Velocity Vector Distillation (DOVD), which aligns the model with a high-fidelity continuous teacher and ground-truth continuous trajectories. This approach drastically improves perceptual quality while preserving prompt adherence and reasoning.

Abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose visual representations into individual features, offering a promising basis for explaining model behavior. Interpreting these features typically relies on images or pixel regions that most strongly activate them. However, this evidence becomes ambiguous when multiple features with different semantics frequently activate in the same locations, such as texture and color in the same patterns. We propose Reconstructive SAE Intervention (RecSAEI), a framework that shifts feature explanation from passive observation to active visual reconstruction. By intervening on representations along SAE decoder directions and reconstructing the visual output, we provide direct evidence of a feature's semantic meaning. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05559v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In biodiversity monitoring, a single image raises several questions: which taxon, how many, which trait, and whether the individual has been seen before. Vision-language models (VLMs) could answer all of these from the image, but their ability is largely untested in biology, as existing benchmarks focus mostly on species identification within a few taxonomic groups. We present Bio-VQA, the largest biological visual question answering (VQA) benchmark and the only one to span four aspects of biological visual understanding: hierarchical taxonomic reasoning, fine-grained attribute grounding, quantitative spatial reasoning, and individual re-identification. Bio-VQA contains 1.86M questions over 217K images from 11 public datasets, and extends right-or-wrong scoring to graded scoring, so a near-miss counts for more than a distant one. Abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) systems serve users across languages and cultural contexts. We find that value-neutral prompts, which admit diverse cultural interpretations, nonetheless yield images that favor particular value orientations, a phenomenon we call visual value leakage. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05593v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can a neural network learn to render 3D Gaussian splats on its own, with no rasterizer in the renderer? We present GaussianRenderFormer, a transformer that takes a set of Gaussians and a camera and outputs the image directly. Each Gaussian becomes one token in a view-independent encoder, and a view-dependent decoder turns small patches of camera rays into pixels by attending to those tokens. Trained on 26,820 Objaverse objects pruned to 20,000 Gaussians each, GaussianRenderFormer renders 300 unseen objects at 38.08 dB PSNR against the full, unpruned splats, while rasterizing the same pruned input reaches 44.02 dB. The gap is not one of generalization, and our diagnostics are consistent with a bottleneck in the view decoder: telling it the projected footprint of each Gaussian, which it could in principle infer, adds 1.4 dB. Under-training is not ruled out. Code, trained models and videos: https://svlwoof.github.io/gaussianrenderformer

articles.title: CAPTOR: text-encoder-free grounding by counting caption co-occurrence over the visual words of a frozen encoder
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05599v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Grounding a text query in an image needs a matrix scoring every term against every patch. Vision-language models compute it with an aligned text encoder, which many image encoders, such as histopathology-related models trained on slides alone, lack. The Caption-Anchored Patch-Term Occurrence Representation (CAPTOR) estimates the matrix without a text encoder. It clusters a frozen image encoder's patch tokens into visual words and describes each captioned image by its share of patches in each word. Abstract: Large language models understand passengers' driving commands, but as driving agents they reason in generated text for seconds and must infer each action's consequences implicitly from the scene. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05507v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humanoid motion tracking has scaled to general policies that reproduce diverse human motion, but the resulting behavior is in free-space: the tracker knows where the body should be, not how it should interact with the environment. Other work makes the object part of the objective, yet abstracts that interaction to contact or geometry, which leaves the demanding cases under-explored. We argue that force is a natural command channel between motion imitation and object interaction, one that specifies not just where to make contact but how hard. We present Ctrl-F, a hierarchical motion-force framework that augments motion tracking with an explicit force command, a 3-D force at each designated contact body such as a hand or a foot. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05567v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Despite growing interest in foundation models for robotic manipulation, systematic evaluation of their capabilities remains elusive. Existing benchmarks are either narrow and saturated, offering little signal on SOTA methods, broadly scoped, providing diversity at the cost of controlled experimentation, or require training on large, messy open-source datasets. We introduce MESA, an evaluation framework designed for precise, reproducible measurement of language-conditioned policy generalization. MESA provides five evaluation suites that isolate in-distribution performance and four distinct axes of generalization: spatial configuration, object instance, object category, and subtask composition, enabling researchers to diagnose where and why policies fail, not just whether they fail. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05571v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robot imitation learning is limited by the scarcity of action-labeled data, while action-free demonstrations such as videos are abundant. Recent latent-action methods learn action-relevant representations from observation transitions, but they do not optimize latent actions for downstream control, leading to latent representations that are difficult for policies to model and difficult to accurately decode into continuous robot actions. This paper introduces ELA, an end-to-end framework for learning from video demonstrations via latent actions jointly optimized for policy learning and action decoding. ELA jointly trains a latent action model, latent action policy, and action decoder, enabling policies to leverage abundant video data with only a handful of action-labeled robot demonstrations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05585v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This letter presents a trajectory planner for humanoid robots to perform dynamic motions on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. The planner generates feasible movements without predefined contact sequences, considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics. To plan bipedal locomotion on steps, ramps, and other terrains, we propose a mathematical model to approximate ground geometry with a smooth surface. The rigid interaction between the robot and the ground is modeled via novel contact constraints, extending the domain of applicability from flat and horizontal surfaces to any arbitrary smooth surface. Abstract: High motion performance and avoiding structural vibrations rely on smooth trajectory planning. For industrial robots, the smoothness requirements have been determined and subsequently taken into account. Although unknown for soft continuum robots, the exact smoothness requirement can potentially be much larger than previously considered ones such as $\mathbf{\mathcal{C}^4}$ for collaborative robots and $\mathbf{\mathcal{C}^5}$ for quadcopter drones. articles.content:

Abstract: This paper presents Proactive Human-in-the-Loop (PHIL), a framework for proactive policy correction and preference-based post-training. PHIL enables operators to preview policy-predicted future motion and intervene before anticipated undesirable actions. During takeover, PHIL continues querying the policy and displaying its predicted trajectories in the physical workspace through an extended reality (XR) interface. PHIL pairs rejected policy predictions with corrective action chunks subsequently executed from the same physical state over the same horizon, and preference-based post-training encourages the policy to favor these corrections. articles.content:

Abstract: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. We introduce OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation. OdorSpaces augments Habitat-Sim with 3D odor transport and dispersion simulated by Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS), enabling agents to navigate photorealistic indoor environments using both visual and olfactory observations. The benchmark includes two representative source-seeking scenarios: invisible gas-leak localization and early-stage fire localization. articles.content:

Abstract: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. In standard bedside assessments, these stimuli are applied manually, resulting in substantial variation in force, duration, frequency, and location. OUCH combines stacked pneumatic pouch actuators, a rigid indenter, and a compliant spacer designed to buckle at a set load, so that the indenter contacts the skin only during actuation. Abstract: We study physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations for robot learning: finding robot controls that reproduce reference motions under contact dynamics. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05793v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. We observe that the optimal correction is often multimodal: when a slower opponent can be passed on either side, good corrections of opposite sign coexist, and the expert's choice between them hinges on tiny cost differences. Deterministic regression then averages modes or inherits inconsistent expert tie-breaking. We propose ZipDrift, which trains a one-step drifting generator over MPC cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations of candidate corrections, without differentiating through the optimiser. Abstract: Assessing the deployment performance of learned robot policies during training is challenging, as directly measuring task success requires costly real-world trials for each candidate checkpoint. Averaged validation loss offers a rollout-free alternative, but its checkpoint rankings can be inconsistent with deployment performance. We analyze two limitations of this criterion: it penalizes action deviations without considering whether the policy can recover from them, and gives later reference predictions equal weight even when earlier deviations may lead execution away from the reference. We propose RACE, a novel rollout-free metric for ranking checkpoints using a fixed set of held-out successful trajectories. Abstract: The optimal rapidly exploring random tree (RRT*) is proven asymptotically optimal on open subsets of Euclidean space with straight-line local planning. Abstract: An ordered sequence of end-effector poses can give a redundant robot arm multiple valid joint configurations at each waypoint. Inverse kinematics (IK) computes these configurations. A learned model removes paths whose transitions are likely to cause self-collision. Abstract: Integrating six-axis tactile feedback into robotic interfaces requires compact sensors with accurate load measurement and rapid online reconstruction. This paper presents LumiTac, a low-profile, camera-free optoelectronic tactile sensor combining spatially distributed illumination with spectral encoding. Abstract: Visual-inertial odometry relies on visual features that correspond to 3D points with consistent projections across sequential frames. articles.title: Learning Object-Centric Motion Priors from Human for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05979v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Manipulating diverse objects with multi-fingered dexterous hands is challenging due to the high dimensionality and complex dynamics. Human-Object Interaction (HOI) datasets provide rich knowledge about task information and embodied interactions. Instead of solely imitating the human demonstrations, our method learns to holistically predict future hand-object states by leveraging these datasets. The predicted future states of the object can serve as a general-purpose reward term for reinforcement learning, reducing reliance on task-specific reward engineering and enhancing generalization across tasks. We conduct extensive experiments on three manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world. Our approach outperforms existing SOTA methods in both success rate and generalizability on novel objects. Furthermore, we validate the cross-embodiment compatibility of our methods by successfully deploying the skills on different robot hands.

articles.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
articles.content: Vision-language-action models are typically built on a simple premise: perception is first compressed by visual encoders, and action reasoning begins only afterwards. Yet manipulation often hinges on precisely the visual signals most vulnerable to this abstraction, e.g., local geometry, boundaries, depth, and subtle state changes. This raises a fundamental question: should action policies inherit a fixed visual endpoint, or directly access evolving visual computation? We introduce NEO-VLA, a structurally encoder-free vision-language-action framework. Images are tokenized by lightweight patch convolutional layers and evolve jointly with language throughout the backbone, allowing a flow-matching action expert to draw from instruction-conditioned visual representations at different depths. This simple change reveals a consistent pattern. Native architectures outperform encoder-based counterparts under controlled comparisons; full fine-tuning reduces but does not erase the gap, and additional scale alone cannot recover it. More strikingly, layer-wise probing shows that the action-critical signals often peak well before the final visual representation. Across diverse manipulation settings and distribution shifts, NEO-VLA consequently achieves stronger and more robust control. Together, these results suggest that embodied control benefits from access to visual representations across the computational hierarchy, rather than a fixed encoder output.

articles.title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
articles.content: Researchers use large language models as agents in social simulations, where agents are prompted with observations and background information intended to shape their actions. Yet LLM agents have been shown to substantially change their behavior under meaning-preserving prompt variations, creating a validation problem for social simulation. One plausible hypothesis is that this brittleness reflects a lack of grounding and can be reduced by enriching the context provided to the agents. Whether richer context improves robustness remains unclear, in part because context richness and robustness are rarely defined in ways that support controlled comparisons. We address the first need with controlled context enrichment, a set of prompt substitution rules that systematically enriches distinct types of context: neutral padding, generic social background, descriptive decision grounding, and normative decision grounding. We address the second by introducing selective robustness as a validation criterion: insensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt variation combined with a directional response to decision-relevant changes in the social world. We demonstrate the framework in a Prisoner's Dilemma-like game, showing how it can be used to identify which forms of context enrichment produce more desirable and robust agent behavior. We find that these forms of enrichment produce distinct behavioral patterns that vary between the two models tested.

articles.title: cuRoboV2-Fast: Fast Torque-Limited Collision-Free Motion Planning
articles.content: We present cuRoboV2-Fast, a GPU-accelerated planner that reduces both planning latency and execution time for collision-free, payload-aware, torque-limited motions. B-spline trajectory optimization reduces the required iterations, while accelerated robot computations and differentiable inverse dynamics reduce refinement cost and accommodate changing payloads. TimeOpt optimizes traversal speed along the fixed path under sampled velocity, acceleration, jerk, and torque constraints, exploiting local spline support to solve banded Newton systems efficiently on the GPU. With a 3,kg payload, cuRoboV2-Fast achieves 4.4 ms mean planning time on RTX 5090, 14.7x faster than cuRoboV2. Our method on Jetson AGX Orin plans faster than cuRoboV1 + TOPPRA on RTX 5090. A stereo-camera-based deployment on YAM achieves 5.93 s mean completed pick-and-drop cycles, 34.6% shorter than cuRoboV2. Code (Apache 2.0): www.github.com/NVlabs/curobo , Project Page: www.research.nvidia.com/labs/lpr/curobov2-fast .

articles.title: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
articles.content: Reconstructing full flow fields from sparse sensors requires prior assumptions about unmeasured regions and physical variables. Yet it remains unclear when learned models outperform classical estimators and which aspects of their predictions can be trusted. FlowReconBench evaluates ten learned and five classical methods on three regimes: a laminar cylinder wake across Reynolds numbers, two-dimensional Kolmogorov turbulence and a large-scale three-dimensional (3D) isotropic turbulence. Methods share leakage-controlled splits and sensor draws and are scored on per-channel error, ensemble spread, calibration, spectra and cost. The leading method changes for each regime. Classical methods perform strongly in low-order and dense-sensing regimes. On the cylinder wake, linear stochastic estimation and gappy proper orthogonal decomposition lead, including for unobserved pressure. In 3D, inverse-distance weighting matches the best learned methods on observed channels. Data-driven methods become superior at decreasing sensor density or poor sensor observability. On Kolmogorov flow, continuous ranked probability score and error yield different method rankings: generative models offer broader but underdispersed ensembles, while deterministic models prioritize pointwise error. Generative models balance this tradeoff through their sampler budget, with a larger budget improving ensemble quality at higher computational cost. In 3D, scaling tests demonstrate that queryable methods are flat in memory, while full-grid construction methods run out of memory. Observing only 2 of 4 fields leaves the problem kinematically underconstrained, yet a latent model can reproduce structural similarities to the ground truth.

articles.title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
articles.content: Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories (SDCLs) are moving chemical experimentation toward embodied automation, where machines must perceive laboratory scenes, reason about experimental states, and act under physical, procedural, and safety constraints. Although Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly considered as embodied brains for such systems, existing laboratory benchmarks mainly focus on safety, anomaly detection, or general scientific understanding, leaving their execution-oriented embodied capabilities underexplored. To fill this gap, we introduce BEAKER, a Benchmark for evaluating Embodied Actionability, Knowledge, Experimentation, and Reasoning in SDCLs. BEAKER contains 1,000 expert-curated question-answer samples across 11 image and video task types, covering key judgments required for chemical laboratory execution, including affordance grounding, trajectory planning, equipment, state, and safety recognition, apparatus setup, operation and step reasoning, and temporal procedure reasoning. All questions and annotations are manually created and reviewed by chemistry and embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) experts, without AI-assisted generation or annotation. We evaluate 28 general-purpose, science-oriented, chemistry-specialized, and embodied MLLMs in an offline, single-turn setting. Results show that current models can follow coarse experimental procedures in videos, but still struggle to ground actions into operable regions and feasible trajectories, to recognize fine-grained laboratory apparatus, states, and safety norms, and to order steps in mid-length procedures. BEAKER thus reveals a clear gap between coarse procedural understanding and the precise, action-grounded perception required for laboratory execution, providing a diagnostic benchmark for future MLLMs in SDCLs.

articles.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
articles.content: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Each task requires agents to review the literature, develop a research plan, conduct research and experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Combining deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics, FrontierPhysics evaluates whether agents' research is correct and publishable. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, no configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts. Manual review of agent trajectories shows that frontier agents' main weaknesses are insufficiently rigorous reasoning and limited expert intuition, rather than gaps in physics knowledge or execution errors.

articles.title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
articles.content: Humanoid robots have the potential to automate a wide range of physical tasks. Progress toward generalist humanoid autonomy, however, remains constrained by a data bottleneck: mapping pixels and free-form language to low-level joint commands requires paired supervision, and no corpus of such data exists at sufficiently large scale. Some approaches rely on human teleoperation and wearable capture devices, which require at least an hour of human time to produce an hour of data. We present HALO, a humanoid autonomy system powered by a pipeline that synthesizes vision-language-motion data across a thousand procedurally generated homes. The corpus scales with compute rather than human labor. HALO acquires a repertoire of physical skills, including sitting on chairs, navigating to named objects, stepping sideways through half-open doors, crouching and crawling beneath tables, and pushing boxes. It orchestrates these skills to solve composite, long-horizon tasks. Without ever seeing a real home during training, HALO transfers zero-shot to the physical world, achieving a 91% success rate across 360 trials in six unmapped real-world environments. See https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-halo/ for code and videos.
